content: Partner 1 sought equal division of bank accounts, securities, and portfolio management in Partner 2’s name at the date separation became final; Partner 2 counterclaimed for similar assets in Partner 1’s name and raised art. 179 issues. The interpretive problems: residual community inclusion of financial instruments, proof of personal origin, and the effect of prior “division” of joint funds. The court held that financial instruments acquired during marriage generally enter community; residual community captures balances existing at dissolution; “de facto” splits do not dissolve the regime. Principles: personal origin requires formal subrogation or clear tracing; absent proof, assets are shared; claims for leasing capitalization fail unless ownership was acquired; the difference due was awarded with interest from the critical date and costs mostly to Partner 2.
